rows.explanation: BKCB2 recommends funding to renovate Bridge Park 3 (B223JC) next to the Farragut NYCHA campus. Specifically: renovate the dilapidated basketball courts and the community garden that has sprung up in the unused bocce courts; reimagine the open space near the handball courts for better community use; and repurpose the underused handball courts as a multiuse hardcourt for affiliated sports including handball, bike polo, pickleball, street soccer, and street hockey. This could be a creative adaptive reuse of concrete areas to benefit multiple demographics at Farragut and the surrounding neighborhood.

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: St. Andrews Park, even in its current condition remains a pivotal recreation destination in the Bedford Stuyvesant community where it resides and for several organizations throughout the borough that also use it. It has the potential to be a jewel of a park. The Board requests the following upgrades: completely reconstruct playground and spray shower; convert asphalt field to a more modern asphalt surface including Mondo perimeter track and fencing; reconstruct basketball & handball courts, adults fitness area, fencing and repair drainage, and; reconstruct comfort station and perimeter sidewalks.
rows.headline: Reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity (i.e. playground, outdoor athletic field)
rows.response: Agency supports and can accommodate Explanation: We have $21.58 million of funding in place for improvements to St. Andrew's Playground through our Community Parks Initiative. The design for the site is expected to be completed in spring 2026 and construction is expected to begin in 2027. For more information, please visit: https://www.nycgovparks.org/planning-and-building/capital-project-tracker/project/10379

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: The tree canopy is large sections of CB3 is severely lacking particularly along many of our commercial corridors (like Fulton Street) and on residential blocks north of Gates Avenue. A robust tree canopy goes a long way to reducing urban heat island effect and in an of climate change, we know that temperatures will only rise. The Board requests new trees planted throughout the district to mitigate for urban heat island effect.
rows.headline: Plant new street trees
rows.response: Agency supports and can accommodate Explanation: As part of our new Neighborhood Tree Planting approach, we will be planting trees in every viable location across the city on a predictable 9-year cycle, prioritizing the most heat-vulnerable neighborhoods first. Find out when we will be planting each neighborhood on the Parks website: https://www.nycgovparks.org/trees/street-tree-planting.
